title: Basic Synchronisation in Go
intro: Basic synchronisation in Go covers the tools you need to coordinate goroutines safely. This module covers sync.WaitGroup for waiting on a group of goroutines (Add before launching, Done with defer in each goroutine, Wait to block until all finish — and the off-by-one mistake that causes panics), sync.Mutex for protecting shared state from concurrent access (Lock/Unlock, defer mu.Unlock() as the safe pattern), the data race definition (two goroutines accessing the same variable concurrently with at least one write — undefined behaviour in Go), the -race flag for detecting races in tests, the select statement for listening on multiple channels simultaneously (how the runtime picks randomly when multiple cases are ready, the default case for non-blocking channel operations), and the done-channel pattern for signalling goroutine shutdown. For freshers, the take-away is: prefer communicating over sharing state, but know the sync primitives when you need them.
